BILL NUMBER: S3065

SPONSOR: RAMOS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the labor law, in relation to requiring training to
reduce abusive conduct and bullying, and cyberbullying in the workplace

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To require all state employees to receive training to prevent abusive
conduct and bullying in all state agencies

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Legislative intent.

Section 2. Adds a new section 27-e to the public officer's law to define
abusive conduct and bullying and requiring all state employees to under-
take prevention training thereon

Section 3: Effective Date: This legislation takes effect 180th day after
enactment.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Issues stemming from the pandemic and the ensuing mental health crisis
are negatively impacting workplaces around the state. According to 2021
survey by the Workplace Bullying Institute, 30% of workers have directly
experienced bullying while at work. People who work remotely were more
likely to report such bullying. with 43% responding that they had been
bullied on the job (https://workplacebullying.orgI2021 -wbi-survey).

As an employer. the state of New York has a responsibility to train its
employees to identify abusive conduct and/or bullying and to educate
staff on the remedies available to affected employees to seek redress
for such actions whether conducted by other employees or managers. This
legislation seeks to address bullying in the worksite by educating
managers and staff about the nature and impact of such conduct and
outlining the processes available.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act takes effect on the 180th day after it becomes law.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3065A

SPONSOR: RAMOS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the labor law, in relation to requiring training to
reduce abusive conduct and bullying, and cyberbullying in the workplace

 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the labor law, in relation to requiring training to
reduce abusive conduct and bullying, and cyberbullying in the workplace

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To require all state employees to receive training to prevent abusive
conduct and bullying in all state agencies

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 would provide the legislative intent.

Section 2 would require the Commissioner of Labor, in consultation with
the Commissioner of Human Rights and representatives of employees, to
develop a written policy statement outlining the responsibility of
respectful conduct by state employees in the workplace as well as a
training program designed to. prevent abusive conduct and bullying in
the workplace for employees.

Such program would include explanations and examples of abusive conduct
and types of bullying, information for employees, and information for
supervisors on addressing incidents of abusive conduct and bullying. The
bill would require state employees to receive such training not later
than one year after the effective date. The provisions would implement
requirements for employers, employees, and employee representatives when
witnessing and reporting such conduct.

The bill would also require the Department of Labor, in conjunction with
representatives of employees, to evaluate and update the criteria and
training as needed.

Section 3 would set the effective date.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):

The amendments would make technical changes clarifying certain
provisions including recordkeeping and reporting requirements. The
amendments would also provide definitions for relevant terms used in the
bill, including "supervisor" and "retaliatory action."

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Issues stemming from the pandemic and the ensuing mental health crisis
are negatively impacting workplaces around the state. According to 2021
survey by the Workplace Bullying Institute, 30% of workers have directly
experienced bullying while at work. People who work remotely were more
likely to report such bullying, with 43% responding that they had been
bullied on the job (https://workplacebullying.org/2021-wbi-survey). As
an employer, the state of New York has a responsibility to train its
employees to identify abusive conduct and/or bullying and to educate
staff on the remedies available to affected employees to seek redress
for such actions whether conducted by other employees or managers.

This legislation seeks to address bullying in the worksite by educating
managers and staff about the nature and impact of such conduct and
outlining the processes available to report and address such issues.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2022 S.9437 (Ramos)/ A.10367 (Joyner)

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act takes effect on the 180th day after it becomes law.

place violence.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 130
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 3065-B, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the labor law, in relation to requiring training to
      reduce abusive conduct and bullying in the workplace"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This  bill would require training to reduce abusive conduct and bully-
ing in the workplace as part of a written workplace violence  prevention
program.
 
  In  New  York,  we  don't  tolerate workplace misconduct. Since taking
office, I have implemented a series of initiatives to  protect  workers,
signing  the  Warehouse Worker Protection Act last year and earlier this
month signing  legislation  allowing  employees  to  file  for  Workers'
Compensation  after  experiencing mental stress. I have also implemented
new policies for State government in particular, including  launching  a
confidential  hotline  and  ensuring all public employees are subject to
our Human Rights Law. This bill, however, does not define  the  specific
conduct  that  is being prohibited, which would likely lead to confusion
for employees, disparate application of the  laws  and  potential  legal
challenges.  My  administration  will  continue to work closely with the
State's public employee unions to address the concerns presented by this
bill.
 
  Therefore, I am constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                       (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                               __________
